stem: What is the $y$-coordinate of the $y$-intercept of the graph of $y = f(x)$ in the $xy$-plane?
stimulus: The graph shows part of the linear function $f$, which a printmaker fitted to measurements from a series of etched plates.

figure.caption: Printmaking: linear function f
figure.alt: A line segment falling from left to right through the points (2, 14), (4, 11), (6, 8) and (8, 5). The segment is drawn only from x = 2 to x = 8.

explanation: The line is not drawn as far as the y-axis, so you have to extend it yourself. Pick two points on the line, such as (2, 14) and (4, 11). The slope is (11 − 14)/(4 − 2) = −3/2. The y-intercept is where x = 0, which is 2 units to the left of (2, 14). Moving 2 units left on a line with slope −3/2 raises y by 3, so the line crosses the y-axis at 14 + 3 = 17.

common_errors.why: Gave the y-value at the left end of the drawn segment (x = 2) and did not extend the line to x = 0.
Used a slope of +3/2 instead of −3/2, so moving left from (2, 14) lowered y by 3 to get 11.
Inverted the slope to −2/3 (run over rise), so moving 2 units left added 4/3 to 14.
Found the x-intercept (where y = 0, at x = 34/3) when the question asked for the y-intercept.

stem: The graph of $y = f(x)$ crosses the $x$-axis at the point $(a, 0)$. What is the value of $a$?
stimulus: The graph shows part of the linear function $f$, which an immunology lab used to model results from its assays.

figure.caption: Immunology: linear function f
figure.alt: A line segment falling from left to right through the points (0, 8), (3, 6), (6, 4) and (9, 2). The segment is drawn only from x = 0 to x = 9.

explanation: You need the x-intercept, which is where y = 0, and the drawn segment stops before it gets there. The line starts at (0, 8). From (0, 8) to (3, 6), y drops 2 for every 3 units to the right, so the slope is −2/3. To fall the full 8 units to the x-axis, the line needs 8 ÷ (2/3) = 12 units to the right. So a = 12.

common_errors.why: Gave the y-intercept, where the line crosses the y-axis, instead of the x-intercept.
Took the right end of the drawn segment as the x-intercept, but y = 2 there, not 0.
Inverted the slope to 3/2 (run over rise) and got 8 ÷ (3/2) = 16/3.

stem: In the $xy$-plane, the graph of $y = mx + b$, where $m$ and $b$ are constants, is shown. What is the value of $b - m$?
stimulus: A marine biologist uses the line shown to summarize a set of reef survey readings.

figure.caption: Marine biology: the graph of y = mx + b
figure.alt: A line falling from left to right through the points (−1, 8), (0, 5), (1, 2), (2, −1) and (3, −4).

explanation: Read the two values separately. The line crosses the y-axis at (0, 5), so b = 5. Step 1 unit right from (0, 5) to (1, 2), and y falls by 3, so m = −3. That makes b − m = 5 − (−3) = 8.

common_errors.why: Took the slope as +3 even though the line falls from left to right, so got 5 − 3 = 2.
Used the x-intercept, 5/3, as b: 5/3 − (−3) = 14/3.
Inverted the slope to −1/3 (run over rise) and got 5 − (−1/3) = 16/3.

stem: What is the $x$-coordinate of the $x$-intercept of the graph of $y = f(x)$ in the $xy$-plane?
stimulus: The graph shows part of the linear function $f$, which a textile historian used to model measurements taken from archived woven samples.

figure.caption: Textile history: linear function f
figure.alt: A line segment rising from left to right through the points (−8, −9), (−4, −6) and (0, −3). The segment is drawn only from x = −8 to x = 0.

explanation: The x-intercept is where y = 0. The drawn segment ends at (0, −3), which is the y-intercept, so you have to extend the line. From (−4, −6) to (0, −3), y rises 3 for every 4 units to the right, so the slope is 3/4. To rise from −3 to 0, y has to go up by 3, which takes 3 ÷ (3/4) = 4 units to the right. The line crosses the x-axis at x = 4.

common_errors.why: Gave the y-intercept, where the drawn segment ends on the y-axis, instead of the x-intercept.
Moved in the wrong direction from (0, −3). A rising line reaches y = 0 to the right of the y-axis, not the left.
Inverted the slope to 4/3 (run over rise) and got 3 ÷ (4/3) = 9/4.

stem: If the graph is extended as a line, what is the value of $f(0)$?
stimulus: For a musicology seminar on tempo, a student plotted the linear function $f$. Its graph is shown for $2 \le x \le 6$.

figure.caption: Graph of $y = f(x)$
figure.alt: A line segment rising from the point (2, 7) through (4, 10) to (6, 13). The segment does not reach the y-axis.

explanation: Read two points off the graph, such as (2, 7) and (4, 10). The slope is $\frac{10 - 7}{4 - 2} = \frac{3}{2}$, so each step 1 to the right raises y by 1.5. To get from x = 2 back to x = 0, you move 2 to the left, so y drops by 3: $f(0) = 7 - 3 = 4$.

common_errors.why: Takes the left end of the drawn segment, f(2), as the y-intercept because it is the lowest point shown.
Gives the slope instead of the value where x = 0.
Uses a slope of -3/2 when moving back to x = 0, so adds 3 to 7 instead of subtracting it.
Finds the slope as run over rise (2/3) and then works out 7 - 2(2/3).

stem: If the graph is extended as a line and $f(a) = 0$, what is the value of $a$?
stimulus: A folklore studies course uses the graph below to introduce linear models. The linear function $f$ is shown for $0 \le x \le 4$.

figure.caption: Graph of $y = f(x)$
figure.alt: A line segment falling from (0, 9) through (1, 7), (2, 5) and (3, 3) to (4, 1).

explanation: The graph crosses the y-axis at (0, 9), so b = 9. Each step 1 to the right takes y down by 2, so the slope is -2 and $f(x) = -2x + 9$. Set $-2a + 9 = 0$ to get $a = 4.5$. The question asks for the x-intercept, not the 9 where the line crosses the y-axis.

common_errors.why: Gives the y-intercept when the question asks where f(x) = 0.
Gives the slope instead of the x-intercept.
Uses a slope of -1/2 (run over rise), so solves -x/2 + 9 = 0.
Takes the last plotted x-value as the crossing point, although y is still 1 there.

stem: The line shown is the graph of $y = ax + b$, where $a$ and $b$ are constants. What is the value of $a + b$?
stimulus: A nutrition science handout includes the following graph.

figure.caption: A line in the xy-plane
figure.alt: A line segment from (0, 8) on the y-axis down to (4, 0) on the x-axis.

explanation: The line crosses the y-axis at (0, 8), so b = 8. From (0, 8) to (4, 0), y falls 8 while x rises 4, so the slope is $a = \frac{0 - 8}{4 - 0} = -2$. Then $a + b = -2 + 8 = 6$.

common_errors.why: Uses a slope of +2 even though the line falls from left to right.
Uses the x-intercept, 4, as b and gets -2 + 4.
Computes the slope as run over rise (-1/2) and gets -1/2 + 8.
Reports b alone and forgets to add a.

stem: If the graph is extended as a line and $g(c) = 0$, what is the value of $c$?
stimulus: A labour economics problem set shows the graph of the linear function $g$ for $1 \le x \le 3$.

figure.caption: Graph of $y = g(x)$
figure.alt: A line segment rising from (1, 2) through (2, 5) to (3, 8).

explanation: From (1, 2) to (2, 5), y rises 3 for each step 1 to the right, so the slope is 3. Moving back from x = 1 to x = 0 takes y down by 3, so $g(0) = -1$ and $g(x) = 3x - 1$. Set $3c - 1 = 0$ to get $c = \frac{1}{3}$.

common_errors.why: Gives the y-intercept instead of the value of x that makes g(x) = 0.
Gives the slope.
Drops a sign when solving 3c - 1 = 0.
Uses a slope of 1/3 (run over rise), so writes y = x/3 + 5/3 and solves for the zero.

Loses the sign when dividing -24 by -4.
Rewrites the equation in slope-intercept form and gives the slope.

stem: If the line shown is extended, it crosses the x-axis at the point $(c, 0)$. What is the value of $c$?

common_errors.why: Gives the y-intercept instead of the x-intercept.

Uses a slope of 2/3 (run over rise) through (4, -3) and solves (2/3)c - 17/3 = 0.
Gives the slope.

stem: The line shown crosses the $y$-axis at the point $(0, b)$. What is the value of $b$?

figure.caption: Fossil Leaf Count by Layer Depth
figure.alt: A straight line segment drawn from (2, 9) through (4, 6) to (6, 3), falling as depth increases. The segment does not reach either axis.

explanation: The drawn segment stops before it reaches the y-axis, so first work out the slope and then extend the line back to x = 0. From (2, 9) to (4, 6), y falls 3 while x rises 2, so the slope is −3/2. Going from x = 2 back to x = 0 is 2 units to the left, so y goes up by 3: 9 + 3 = 12. Check it with the equation $y = -\tfrac{3}{2}x + 12$: at x = 6, y = −9 + 12 = 3. So b = 12.

common_errors.why: Extended the line the other way to where it meets the x-axis, at (8, 0), and gave the x-intercept instead of the y-intercept.
Took the y-value of the leftmost plotted point, (2, 9), as the intercept without extending the line back to x = 0.
Used a slope of +3/2 instead of −3/2, so going 2 units left subtracted 3 from 9 when it should have added 3.
Gave the slope of the line, not its y-intercept.

stem: The line shown crosses the $x$-axis at the point $(a, 0)$. What is the value of $a$?

figure.caption: Antibody Level After a Booster Dose
figure.alt: A straight line segment drawn from (1, 2) through (2, 5) to (3, 8), rising as weeks increase. The segment does not reach either axis.

explanation: Read two points that sit exactly on gridlines, (1, 2) and (2, 5). The slope is (5 − 2)/(2 − 1) = 3. Going 1 unit left from (1, 2) to x = 0 lowers y by 3, so the y-intercept is −1 and the line is $y = 3x - 1$. The x-intercept is where y = 0: 3a − 1 = 0, so a = 1/3. That fits the picture, since the line would cross the x-axis just to the right of the origin, a little before x = 1.

common_errors.why: Found the y-intercept, −1, and gave that when the question asked where the line crosses the x-axis.
Solved 3a − 1 = 0 as a = −1/3, getting the sign wrong when moving the constant across.
Gave the slope of the line instead of the x-intercept.
Took the leftmost plotted point, (1, 2), as the point where the line meets the axis, without extending the line down to y = 0.

stem: The graph of $y = h(x)$ is shown, where $h(x) = mx + b$ and $m$ and $b$ are constants. What is the value of $m$?

figure.caption: Altitude of a Rising Star
figure.alt: A straight line drawn from (2, 0) through (4, 5) and (6, 10) to (8, 15), rising from left to right.

explanation: m is the slope, so pick two points that land exactly on gridlines, such as (2, 0) and (4, 5). Going 2 units to the right, the line rises 5, so m = rise ÷ run = 5/2. The line rises from left to right, so m has to be positive. Check it with another pair of points: from (4, 5) to (8, 15), the line rises 10 over a run of 4, and 10/4 = 5/2.

common_errors.why: Divided the run by the rise instead of the rise by the run.
Gave the x-intercept, read where the line meets the x-axis at (2, 0), instead of the slope.
Extended the line back to x = 0 and gave the y-intercept, b = −5, instead of m.
Read the rise of 5 between (2, 0) and (4, 5) but forgot to divide by the run of 2.
Got the steepness right but gave the slope a negative sign, even though the line rises from left to right.
